nodes.title: Pointwise control of approximation error
nodes.informalSketch: The average of numbers each at most $\varepsilon$ is at most $\varepsilon$. Multiply the resulting sum bound by $n^{-1}$.

nodes.title: Finite-sample expressivity on the spike
nodes.informalSketch: Open target. The finite-sample interpolation argument is not yet formalized.

nodes.title: Hidden features
nodes.informalSketch: The readout identity is the definition of \texttt{forward}, unfolded.

nodes.title: Alignment is non-negative
nodes.informalSketch: Both the numerator and the denominator are sums of squares. The zero-matrix case returns $0$.

nodes.title: Alignment is at most one
nodes.informalSketch: By symmetry $P^\top=P$ and idempotence $P^2=P$, each row $i$ satisfies $\sum_j ((HP)_{ij})^2 = \sum_j (HP)_{ij} H_{ij}$. Expanding $\lVert H - HP\rVert_F^2$ row by row yields the exact Frobenius Pythagorean identity $\lVert H - HP\rVert_F^2 = \lVert H\rVert_F^2 - \lVert HP\rVert_F^2$. Since $\lVert H - HP\rVert_F^2 \ge 0$, $\lVert HP\rVert_F^2 \le \lVert H\rVert_F^2$, so dividing by $\lVert H\rVert_F^2 > 0$ gives $a(H,P)\le 1$.

nodes.title: Alignment certificate
nodes.informalSketch: From the Frobenius Pythagorean identity $\lVert H - HP\rVert_F^2 = \lVert H\rVert_F^2 - \lVert HP\rVert_F^2 = (1 - a(H,P))\lVert H\rVert_F^2$, the lower bound $a(H,P)\ge 1-\varepsilon$ immediately yields $\lVert H - HP\rVert_F^2 \le \varepsilon \lVert H\rVert_F^2$.

nodes.title: Exponential approach under a descent rate
nodes.informalSketch: Define the rescaled excess risk $g(s) = e^{cs}(L(s)-F)$. By the product and chain rules, $g'(s) = e^{cs}(c(L(s)-F) + L'(s)) \le 0$ for all $s\in\mathbb{R}$. Monotonicity of functions with nonpositive derivative (`image_le_of_deriv_right_le_deriv_boundary`) yields $g(t)\le g(0) = L(0)-F$ for $t\ge 0$, and multiplying by $e^{-ct}>0$ completes the proof.

nodes.title: Activation Lipschitz bound
nodes.informalSketch: Immediate from the Lipschitz field of \cref{def:activation}.

nodes.title: Lipschitz bound for one layer
nodes.informalSketch: Apply the finite-sum Cauchy--Schwarz inequality (`Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq`) to $\langle w, x\rangle - \langle w, y\rangle = \langle w, x-y\rangle$ to obtain $|\langle w,x\rangle - \langle w,y\rangle| \le \|w\|_2\|x-y\|_2$, and compose with the activation Lipschitz bound $|\sigma(a)-\sigma(b)|\le L|a-b|$.

nodes.title: Lipschitz bound for the network
nodes.informalSketch: Apply the triangle inequality to the sum over hidden units $i\in\mathrm{Fin}\,m$, bound each unit by $|W_{2,i}|\,L\,\|W_{1,i}\|_2\,\|x-y\|_2$ using \cref{lem:layer_lipschitz}, and factor out $\|x-y\|_2$.

nodes.title: Bounded empirical means
nodes.informalSketch: Triangle inequality for finite sums and $|a_i|\le 1$ give $\bigl|\sum a_i\bigr|\le n$. Multiply by the positive scalar $n^{-1}$.

nodes.title: Rademacher symmetrization
nodes.informalSketch: Open target. Do not tag this proof \texttt{\textbackslash leanok} until \texttt{sorry} is gone. \cref{lem:bounded_mean} is the intended elementary input.

nodes.title: Spectral norm of Gaussian projections
nodes.informalSketch: Open target (concentration of measure).

nodes.title: Spectral bias in $\mup$ scaling
nodes.informalSketch: Combine $e^{2\gamma_{\mathrm{bulk}}t} = e^{2(\gamma_{\mathrm{bulk}}-\gamma_{\mathrm{lead}})t} e^{2\gamma_{\mathrm{lead}}t} \le e^{-2\Delta\gamma t} e^{2\gamma_{\mathrm{lead}}t}$ with the signal and bulk bounds in continuous time, and compare $1+\eta\gamma_{\mathrm{lead}} \ge 1+\eta\gamma_{\mathrm{bulk}} + \eta\Delta\gamma$ in discrete time. Apply the Frobenius Pythagorean identity $\lVert H\rVert_F^2 = \lVert HP\rVert_F^2 + \lVert H-HP\rVert_F^2$ to lower-bound $a(H,P)$ by $1 - B/S$, and invoke Lemma~\ref{lem:feature_learning_advantage} for the multi-step ridge MSE improvement.

nodes.title: Representation contraction in residual blocks
nodes.informalSketch: Bound each coordinate of $\sigma(Wx)-\sigma(Wy)$ via Cauchy--Schwarz and $L_\sigma$-Lipschitzness, square and sum over rows to obtain $\|\sigma(Wx)-\sigma(Wy)\|_2 \le L_\sigma\|W\|_F\|x-y\|_2$, and apply the Euclidean triangle inequality to $x + \alpha\sigma(Wx)$. Induct over $L$ layers and apply $(1+c/L)^L \le (e^{c/L})^L = e^c$.

nodes.title: Global feature-learning alignment
nodes.informalSketch: Apex target. Bounty \$15000. Requires the preceding open lemmas.

nodes.title: Population risk adds
nodes.informalSketch: Add the two inequalities.

nodes.title: Finite-data ridge training
nodes.informalSketch:
Identify the actual gradient using Mathlib calculus. Positive regularization makes
the finite-dimensional Hessian injective and hence surjective, giving a stationary
point. Quadratic expansion proves minimization. Apply TorchLean's strongly monotone
Lipschitz-operator gradient-descent theorem.

nodes.title: Reused neural semantics and global bounds
nodes.informalSketch:
Reuse TorchLean's Euclidean tensor metric, matrix Frobenius bound and ReLU
Lipschitz theorem; compose with Mathlib's Lipschitz lemmas. Expand coordinates
for the legacy correspondence. No differentiability of ReLU at zero is assumed.

nodes.title: Exact masked attention bounds
Population-risk envelopes
nodes.informalSketch:
Bound the squared error pointwise using the triangle inequality and Lipschitz
or convex-combination bounds. Dominate it by an integrable envelope and apply
monotonicity and linearity of the Bochner integral.

nodes.title: Conditional empirical-risk oracle bridge
nodes.informalSketch:
Identify the risk normalizations and apply FoML's deterministic
approximate-ERM oracle inequality. Integrability follows by bounded domination.

nodes.title: Finite-class uniform deviation
nodes.informalSketch:
Identify OpenTheory's supervised risks with StatLean's definitions, then reuse
its sub-Gaussian Hoeffding bound and finite-union argument.

nodes.title: Ridge objective convergence
nodes.informalSketch:
Expand the quadratic at the stationary minimizer, bound $\|A v\|$ by
$\|A\|\|v\|$, and compose with the checked TorchLean distance rate.

nodes.title: Learning by finite model selection
nodes.informalSketch:
Use Mathlib's finite minimum theorem, then contain the excess-risk event in
StatLean's finite-class uniform-deviation event.

nodes.title: Continuous-class cover transfer
nodes.informalSketch:
Each covered loss differs from its representative by at most $\rho$ in both
empirical and population risk. Contain the bad event in StatLean's finite-class
event. Reuse Mathlib's compact finite-ball cover for existence.

nodes.title: A fixed ball for ridge training
nodes.informalSketch:
Compare the minimizer's objective with the objective at zero. The geometric
distance bound never exceeds the initial distance, and the triangle inequality
gives the iterate radius. Bound mean squared labels by $T^2$.

nodes.title: Trained ridge excess risk
nodes.informalSketch:
The uniform step is admissible for every design whose rows are bounded by $B$,
and the resulting contraction is at most $q$. A minimizer is the unique
stationary point, so the distance bound and the quadratic expansion control the
regularized gap. A floor grid, radially projected onto the ball, is a finite
net; the finite-class Hoeffding bound transfers across that net. Product
samples that leave the bounded set have measure zero.

nodes.title: Fixed-design ridge degrees of freedom
nodes.informalSketch:
A minimizer is the unique stationary point, so the gradient-descent limit equals
the ridge solution. The prediction error splits into a regularization bias and
the hat operator applied to the noise. The bias quadratic form is at most
$\lambda/(4c)$ times $\|\theta_\star\|^2$; with $c=1/m$, dividing by $m$ leaves
$(\lambda/4)\|\theta_\star\|^2$. The hat operator is self-adjoint with
eigenvalues in $[0,1]$, so its trace is at most its number of nonzero
eigenvalues, which is at most the rank of $A$. White noise has mean zero, so
the cross term integrates to zero, and the expected noise energy is $\sigma^2$
times the sum of squared eigenvalues, hence at most $\sigma^2$ times the
degrees of freedom.

nodes.title: Kernel form of ridge
nodes.informalSketch:
The operators satisfy $(K+\lambda I)A=A(cA^*A+\lambda I)$. Inverting and
composing with $A^*$ identifies the primal predictor with the kernel smoother.
Equal kernels determine the same smoother. The range of $AA^*$ equals the range
of $A$, and a nonzero scalar does not change that range. Rewrite the
fixed-design integral through the prediction identity.

nodes.title: One-step feature displacement
nodes.informalSketch: The partial derivative of the half-squared loss in a first-layer entry is the residual times the readout coordinate, the activation derivative and the corresponding input coordinate. Summing the resulting entrywise updates against the input produces the preactivation identity. The three rates are the absolute value of that identity under the corresponding bounds on the readout.

nodes.title: Tangent step and ridge perturbation
nodes.informalSketch: Substitute the exact preactivation step into the first-order output formula. The difference from the updated network is a sum of activation remainders. Apply the mean value theorem on the segment from the old preactivation to the new one, and use the Lipschitz bound on $\sigma'$. Sum the resulting coordinate bounds under each learning-rate hypothesis. For the ridge comparison, expand $\|p-t\|^2$ by the triangle inequality and replace the cross term using $2ab\le a^2+b^2$. Integrate and insert the fixed-design bound.

nodes.title: Single-input nonlinear trajectory and centered ridge endpoint
nodes.informalSketch: Bound the Frobenius norm of each first-layer update by Cauchy--Schwarz and induction on $t$. Derive the preactivation shift and output residual envelopes from the parameter norm. Combine the one-step output remainder and slope drift with the scalar linear contraction recurrence to bound the $T$-step trajectory gap, add the geometric optimization residual $q^T|f_0(x)-y|$, and integrate against the discrete noise distribution.

nodes.title: Multi-observation nonlinear MLP trajectory and fixed-design statistical risk
nodes.informalSketch: Flatten the $m\times d$ displacement matrix via $\mathrm{finProdFinEquiv}$ so the multi-row linearized forward pass equals $F_0+J_0 u$. Bound the operator norm of the shifted Jacobian design at every step by $\sqrt{n}\sqrt{m}A L\sqrt{E}$ and induct on $t$ to obtain the closed norm, preactivation-shift, and residual envelopes from $\|F_0-y\|_2\le S$. Decompose each parameter step difference $u_{t+1}-v_{t+1}$ into the nonexpansive linear ridge step applied to $u_t-v_t$ plus the adjoint-residual Taylor and Jacobian-drift defect $(\eta/n)(\|J_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}B+G R)$. Sum the defects over $T$ steps, convert parameter distance to output distance via $B+\|J_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|u_T-v_T\|_2$, and combine with geometric ridge GD convergence $\|v_T-u_\star^{\mathrm{ridge}}\|_2\le q^{T/2}S/\sqrt{n\lambda}$. Finally, apply the pointwise quadratic perturbation bound $\|p-t\|_2^2\le 2\|q-t\|_2^2+2\delta^2$ and integrate against the fixed-design ridge degrees-of-freedom theorem.

nodes.title: Horizon-free contractive MLP trajectory and statistical risk
nodes.informalSketch: Combine the operator-norm bound on the shifted Jacobian with the output-change bound to establish the one-step affine norm recurrence $\|u_{t+1}\|_2 \le q_{\mathrm{nl}}\|u_t\|_2 + c_{\mathrm{nl}}S$. Induct on $t$ using $q_{\mathrm{nl}}<1$ to obtain the geometric fixed-point bound $U_\infty$, and deduce the time-uniform shift and residual envelopes $D_\infty$ and $R_\infty$. Use strict contraction of the strongly convex ridge GD step (`Optim.GD.step_norm_sq_le` and `Optim.GD.q_lt_one_of_mul_sq_lt`) to sum the one-step defects as a convergent geometric series bounded by $\delta_{\mathrm{step}}/(1-q_{\mathrm{gd}})$. Combine with geometric convergence to the ridge solution and integrate via `PredictionGap.sq_norm_le_double` and `MLPFixedDesign.ridge_expected_mse`.

nodes.title: Feature-learning advantage over frozen initial kernels
nodes.informalSketch: Specialize `FeatureStep.preactivation_step` to $f_0(x)=0$, $W_{2,i}=s_i/m$, and $\eta_1=m$ to cancel $m$ and obtain the exact shift $y\alpha s_i\|x\|_2^2$. Expand $(p_i + \Delta\mathrm{pre}_i)^2 - p_i^2$ and sum over neurons to establish strict kernel growth. Evaluate the centered ridge objective and finite-noise expected MSE at `MLPEndpoint.ridgeWeights`, put the difference of rational functions over the common denominator $(K_0+\lambda)^2(K_1+\lambda)^2$, and apply positivity under the signal-to-noise threshold. Combine with the Frobenius Pythagorean identity from Lemma~\ref{lem:alignment_le_one} for the subspace residual reduction.

nodes.title: Multi-head attention ablation fidelity, residual propagation, and risk transfer
nodes.informalSketch: Split the full sum over $\mathrm{Fin}\,H$ into $\mathrm{keep}$ and $\mathrm{keep}^c$ via `Finset.sum_add_sum_compl`. Bound each ablated head's row output by $B_{V,h}$ using `Attention.rowOutput_norm_le` and apply the continuous linear operator norm bound $\|W_{O,h}(u)\| \le \|W_{O,h}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|u\|$. Propagate through $G$ by Lipschitz continuity and through $L$ residual stages by induction on $L$. For the population risk bound, apply `PredictionGap.sq_norm_le_double` pointwise a.e. and integrate against $P.\mathrm{law}$.

nodes.title: Local-sharpness adaptive descent, objective coercivity, and discrete PL convergence
nodes.informalSketch: Complete the square in $\eta$ to prove optimality of $\eta^\star = 1/S_{\mathrm{loc}}$. For coercivity, drop each nonnegative term in $\frac{1}{2n}\|F(u_t)-y\|_2^2 + \frac{\lambda}{2}\|u_t\|_2^2 \le \frac{S^2}{2n}$ to bound $\|F(u_t)-y\|_2$ and $\|u_t\|_2$ directly, and apply Cauchy--Schwarz for the preactivation shift. For PL convergence, substitute $\|g_t\|_2^2 \ge 2\mu(L(u_t)-F)$ into the optimal drop $L(u_{t+1}) \le L(u_t) - \|g_t\|_2^2/(2 S_{\mathrm{loc}}(t))$ and induct on $T$.

nodes.title: Trajectory-localized out-of-sample generalization bound
nodes.informalSketch: Write $f_u(x) - f_v(x)$ as the forward change from base network $\mathrm{atDisplacement}(\mathrm{net}, v)$ under displacement $u-v$, bound preactivation shifts by $\|u-v\|_2\sqrt{E}$, and apply `MLPResidual.forward_change_le` to obtain $|f_u(x)-f_v(x)| \le m A L\sqrt{E}\|u-v\|_2$. Combine with `BallCover.euclideanBall_net` to construct the finite loss cover of $B_{md}(R)$ and apply `Covering.uniform_deviation_tail` and `Covering.approx_learner_tail`.

nodes.title: Softmax score sensitivity, joint Q/K/V stability, and logit-margin concentration
nodes.informalSketch:
Since $\sum_i p(s_1,m)_i = \sum_i p(s_2,m)_i = 1$, subtracting $\sum_i (p_1(i)-p_2(i)) ar{v} = 0$ rewrites the output difference in terms of centered values $v_i -  ar{v}$, yielding the $\Delta_V\|p_1-p_2\|_1$ bound by the triangle inequality. For a dominant key $i_\star$, rewrite $\mathrm{rowOutput}(s,m,v) - v_{i_\star} = \sum_{j
e i_\star} p_j(v_j - v_{i_\star})$ and use $\sum_{j
e i_\star} p_j = 1 - p_{i_\star} \le \varepsilon$. Under a logit margin $\gamma$, `Attention.weight_formula` gives $\exp(s_j) \le e^{-\gamma}\exp(s_{i_\star})$ on unmasked keys $j
e i_\star$, and summing over the $n-1$ non-dominant keys bounds the tail mass by $(n-1)e^{-\gamma}$.

nodes.title: First-principles MLP local sharpness and unconditional coercive trajectory
nodes.informalSketch: Decompose $F(u+\Delta) - y = r_u + (J_u\Delta + \mathrm{rem})$ around the shifted network $\mathrm{atDisplacement}(\mathrm{net}, u)$. Bound $\|J_u\Delta + \mathrm{rem}\|_2 \le \sqrt{n} m A L\sqrt{E}\|\Delta\|_2$ via `MLPBatchBounds.batchOutput_change_le` and $\|\mathrm{rem}\|_2 \le \sqrt{n} M m A E\|\Delta\|_2^2$ via `MLPBatchBounds.output_remainder_le`. Expand $\|r_u + (J_u\Delta + \mathrm{rem})\|_2^2$ and $\|u+\Delta\|_2^2$ using `norm_add_sq_real`, identify the linear term $\langle \nabla\mathcal{L}(u), \Delta\rangle$ via adjointness of $J_u$, and bound $\langle r_u, \mathrm{rem}\rangle \le R\|\mathrm{rem}\|_2$ by Cauchy--Schwarz. Induct on $t$ using Lemma~\ref{lem:local_sharpness_descent}: at each step $\mathcal{L}(u_t)\le \mathcal{L}(0)$ implies $\|r_{u_t}\|_2\le S$, which keeps the local sharpness bounded by $S_{\mathrm{MLP}}(S)$ for step $t+1$. Telescope the one-step drops to bound the minimum squared gradient norm over $T$ steps.

nodes.title: Diagonal preconditioned and SignGD/Adam-style optimization speedup
nodes.informalSketch: Complete the square coordinate by coordinate to establish $\sum_i g_i^2/(2S_i) - \mathrm{coordProgress}(\eta,S,g) = \sum_i \frac{S_i}{2}(\eta_i - 1/S_i)^2 g_i^2 \ge 0$. Combine fractions over $2 S_i S_{\max}$ for the scalar SGD comparison and apply `Finset.sum_pos'` when an active coordinate has $S_{i_0} < S_{\max}$. For SignGD, use $\mathrm{sign}(x)x = |x|$ and $\mathrm{sign}(x)^2 \le 1$ to obtain the quadratic bound in $\eta$ and substitute $\eta_{\mathrm{sign}} = \|g\|_1/\|S\|_1$.
